name: Combined Immunodeficiency Due to DOCK8 Deficiency

ethnicAssociations: Higher prevalence in populations with consanguinity
Reported in diverse ethnic groups including Middle Eastern and European descent

criteria.description: Biallelic pathogenic variants in the DOCK8 gene confirmed by molecular genetic testing
Profound lymphopenia with markedly reduced CD4+ and CD8+ T cells and impaired antibody responses
Recurrent viral, bacterial, and fungal infections with severe atopy and eczema
Peripheral blood eosinophilia and elevated serum IgE levels
Consanguinity or affected siblings with similar immunodeficiency phenotype

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of biallelic pathogenic DOCK8 variants plus clinical immunodeficiency features and immunophenotyping abnormalities
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires integration of genetic, immunologic, and clinical data; exclusion of other combined immunodeficiencies is essential

occasional.symptomName: Squamous cell carcinoma of the vulva

laboratory: Marked lymphopenia with low CD4+ and CD8+ T cell counts
Elevated serum IgE and peripheral eosinophilia
imaging: Chest radiographs showing recurrent pneumonia or bronchiectasis
MRI brain in cases with neurological complications
other: Flow cytometry showing defective T cell proliferation and NK cell function

distinguishingFeatures: STAT3 mutations with skeletal abnormalities and retained IgE elevation
Characteristic facial features and dental abnormalities absent in DOCK8 deficiency
Profound T cell deficiency with absent thymic shadow
Early infancy presentation with severe opportunistic infections
Eczema and immunodeficiency but with bleeding tendency

redFlags: Severe recurrent viral skin infections resistant to standard therapy
Early onset severe eczema with elevated IgE and eosinophilia
Recurrent life-threatening bacterial and fungal infections
references: Zhang Q, Davis JC, Lamborn IT, et al. Combined immunodeficiency associated with DOCK8 mutations. N Engl J Med. 2009;361(21):2046-2055.
Engelhardt KR, McGhee S, Winkler S, et al. Large deletions and point mutations involving DOCK8 in the autosomal-recessive form of hyper-IgE syndrome. J Allergy Clin Immunol. 2009;124(6):1289-1302.e4.
Orange JS, Glessner JT, Resnick E, et al. Genome-wide association identifies diverse causes of common variable immunodeficiency. J Allergy Clin Immunol. 2011;127(6):1360-1367.
